paper_metadata.title: Influence of molybdenum contents on the microstructure, mechanical properties and oxidation behavior of multi-elemental Nb-Si based ultrahigh temperature alloys

evidence.quote: Influence of molybdenum contents on the microstructure, mechanical properties and oxidation behavior of multi-elemental Nb – Si based ultrahigh temperature alloys

Four multi-elemental Nb – Si based ultrahigh temperature alloys with compositions of Nb – 22Ti – 15Si – 5Cr – 3Al – 3V-2Hf-2Zr- x Mo ( x = 0, 2, 5 and 10 at.%) were prepared by vacuum non-consumable arc melting under an argon atmosphere in a water cooled copper crucible (these alloys are respectively referred to as 0Mo, 2Mo, 5Mo and 10Mo alloys for convenience).

In order to minimize the impact of uncontrollable factors and get homogeneous button ingots, the melting process for each button ingot must satisfy the following requirements: (i) The surface impurities and oxide films of raw materials were removed by acid/ alkaline cleaning; (ii) The same maximum melting current and the same cooling conditions were guaranteed for each melting cycle; (iii) All the four ingots were re-melted at least 3 times.

parameters.cooling_method: furnace cooled to room temperature at 5 °C/min

evidence.quote: Two cubic specimens for each alloy with size of 7 × 7 × 7 mm3 were prepared for isothermal oxidation at 1250 ◦C. … The furnace was firstly heated up to 450 ◦C with a rate of 10 ◦C/min, then was further heated up to 1250 ◦C with a rate of 27 ◦C/min. After holding for 1 or 20 h at 1250 ◦C, the furnace was cooled down to room temperature with a rate of 5 ◦C/min.

it is suggested that slightly increased concentration of Mo in primary silicide blocks has a stronger effect of solid solution strengthening.
This is mainly attributed to a large amount of Mo dissolved in Nbss which generate a stronger solid solution strengthening, as well as the increased microhardness of silicides in eutectics.

the crack propagation in the 2Mo alloy, which has the highest fracture toughness KQ value, possesses higher frequencies of crack deflection, branching and bridging that can consume more energy for crack growth and then improve the room-temperature fracture toughness of the alloys.

the volatilization of MoO3 introduces lots of small holes … these holes provide the space for oxide expansion and thus the growth stress is released to some extent. This is propitious for the primary silicides to move gradually and decrease its cracking tendency, in turns to improve the adhesion of oxide scales.

the higher Mo content addition in the alloys also introduces excessive holes in the scales, which provide diffusion path of O2 and is responsible for the deterioration of the oxidation resistance of 5Mo and 10Mo alloys
